content.title: Is it Really Possible to Watch Coachella at Home? Yes — Here’s How
content.text: If you can’t make it to Coachella, don’t worry — Coachella can come to you.The 25th edition of the famed Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival, which takes place at the Empire Polo Club in Indio, California, kicks off April 10. A wide range of stars will perform, including Justin Bieber, Sabrina Carpenter, Teddy Swims and Karol G.The event runs over two weekends. The first is April 10, 11 and 12, followed by April 17, 18 and 19. This year’s event will also be available to watch at home, so if you don’t plan to trek to the desert, you can slip into your jammies, fire up your computer or phone and still take in what the festival’s musical acts have to offer.How to Watch Coachella At Home For FreeThe festival’s performances will be available to stream on YouTube. Head to Coachella’s page and scroll to the stage you’d like to watch, or click here for a playlist of all the available livestreams, which are set to start at 4 p.m. PT on April 10. In addition to the main stage, or the Coachella Stage, shows will be held on seven other stages: Outdoor Theatre, Sahara, Mojave, Gobi, Sonora and Quasar.Here’s the Full Coachella ScheduleThere are some real heavyweights who will take the main Coachella stage. (All times are PT.)Sabrina Carpenter will perform from 9:05 p.m. until 10:35 p.m. on April 10. She will be followed at midnight by electronic artist Anyma. Teddy Swims will perform earlier in the night at 5:30 p.m.Bieber will headline on April 11 with an 11:25 p.m. show. That will wrap up a night that features performances from other acts such as The Strokes at 9 p.m. and Addison Rae at 5:30 p.m.The final night on April 12 will culminate with Karol G’s 9:55 p.m. set. Young Thug will perform before her at 7:50 p.m. The whole livestream schedule is available here.You can check the entire Coachella schedule for a list of all the talent performing, as well as what stage they’ll be on and what time their sets begin. More highlights include Katseye at 8 p.m. Friday on the Sahara stage, Sombr at 7:05 p.m. Saturday at the Outdoor Theatre, FKA Twigs at 8:45 p.m. Sunday on the Mojave stage and more.The schedule for the second weekend is not yet available.
